item.subject: science
item.stem:
Meena throws a ball straight up into the air in her school playground. The ball slows down, stops for a moment, and then falls back to the ground, speeding up as it comes down.
Which statement correctly explains the motion of the ball?

options.A: The Earth pulls the ball towards itself with an attractive gravitational force, which slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down.
options.B: The ball carries an upward force from the throw until this force runs out, and the Earth pulls the ball only after it starts falling.
options.C: The Earth's gravitational force acts only when the ball is touching the ground, so the ball slows down on its own while going up.
options.D: The Earth pushes the ball upwards while it rises and pulls it downwards only at the highest point.
